"THE REBELLION IS WAITING" and "WAD BERLIN 2025 · ARCADE AREA · BOOTH ENTIRE.IO" are now near-peers: both mono, both uppercase, both letterspaced, similar size, both containing bright white. So the story voice (tagline) and the event metadata (brand line) read as one blob, and your eye doesn't know which matters. On the mockup the brand line was clearly a whisper; we lost that when I brightened it. The fix isn't to shrink it back to illegible — it's to keep it readable but give the tagline a clear step up (bigger, white) while the brand line stays a step down (smaller, gray, only "WAD BERLIN 2025" popping).

Good rhythm would be: eyebrow tight to the title (they're one unit), a bigger breath before the tagline, the brand line hanging closer to the tagline but visually quieter, then a generous gap (~56px) before the CTA row so the buttons feel like their own zone. Right now the whole column reads as evenly-stacked lines. OPTIONS also sits a bit close to the scanline footer — a touch more separation would keep the footer feeling like chrome rather than a fourth menu item.

Concretely I'd do: title→tagline gap 14→26px, tagline→brand gap 10→12px but brand line down to ~13–15px secondary gray, menu margin 44→56px, OPTIONS gap under CTAs 18→26px, and nudge the scanline lower. That gives you three clear zones — identity, message, action — instead of seven lines.
